proposed_from.topic: Corrected terminal-row compatibility and the covariance information frontier for soft-intervention linear causal disentanglement. For every 2<=p<=q and q-node DAG G, observe one baseline and one unknown-target single-node soft-intervention context per latent node in X^(k)=F(I-Lambda^(k))^-1 epsilon^(k), with full-row-rank mixing, noncollinear columns, exact nonzero graph support, independent non-Gaussian errors, and algebraically independent nonzero incoming-edge changes. Define Hsoft(G) from the actual intervention rows h_k^T=delta_k^T(I-Lambda^0)^-1, not the published observational-path substitution, with exact support and noncancellation admissibility; define Cov_p(G) by generic positive-real covariance compatibility. Prove: (1) a sound-and-complete terminal-copy strict-gammoid plus affine-hyperplane certificate algorithm for Hsoft and an exact characterization of when the published Definition 3.14 class agrees; (2) Cov_q(G)=Hsoft(G) under square mixing by whitening and ancestor-order recovery, including all sign, scale, support, and variance branches; and (3) for p<q, a graph-specific non-QE positive-real projection-completeness criterion deciding Cov_p(G)\Hsoft(G), with generic realization or separator certificates, explicit complexity, and infinite equality and strict families. Credit Leyes Carreno--Meroni--Seigal 2025 Theorem 1.7, Definition 3.14, and Problems 5.1--5.2, and Squires et al. 2023 for injective soft-intervention transitive-closure recovery. The companion LCD workflow is a prospective same-question consumer: it must report the corrected compatible DAG set and whether high cumulants genuinely remove covariance alternatives. PRESOLVE EVIDENCE REQUIRING VERIFICATION: Exact symbolic checks give a generic four-node determinant gamma(beta*d-b*delta) refuting the observational-path substitution, five positive-definite square covariances, and a separate p=2 rational covariance collision with actual-row obstruction -2. Terminal-copy linkage and affine support testing, square covariance equality, an infinite small-component equality family, and a complete regular reduction of the four-node noninjective fork to eight two-scalar positive systems were derived. A stronger rational collision keeps candidate variances T+144/121 and 19/4 positive for every T>0, T!=1. Classical-linkage, generic-QE, degenerate-rank, all-sign/variance-chamber, rational-certificate, finite-sample, consumer-deployment, and bounded-literature failure modes were checked; the all-p positive chamber union remains open. UNRESOLVED BOTTLENECK: Prove a graph-specific, non-QE positive-real projection-completeness criterion deciding whether the finite union of every legal covariance branch has complement of empty relative interior in the full true parameter domain. EARLY KILL TEST: Complete the eight-branch two-scalar positive-feasibility classification of the four-node p=2 fork over its full true parameter domain and verify every proposed separator against the original context covariance equations; pivot if the structured reduction is unsound or generalizes only through unrestricted quantifier elimination. proposed_from.novelty_justification: Problem 5.2 and Proposition 3.6 of Leyes Carreno, Meroni, and Seigal (2025) motivate the destination: they do not classify which distinct DAGs survive every legal positive-real covariance branch under noninjective soft interventions. The class \(\mathsf{Cov}_p(G)\) is a robust generic-chamber refinement, is definitionally contained in \(\mathsf{soft2M}_{2,p}(G)\), and is not identified with the published covariance-compatible class. Zhang, Greenewald, Squires et al. recover an equivalence class from unpaired observational and interventional data under generalized faithfulness, but neither give nor rule out this noninjective positive-real covariance frontier. The closest methods also include the semidefinite and positive-semidefinite realization machinery of Kela et al., the affine-birational constraint-transfer results of Boege and Solus, the half-trek criteria of Foygel Barber et al., and the primal-treewidth quantifier-elimination framework of Wu et al. None supplies a finite non-birational branch union coupled through one mixing matrix and one structural inverse with a dense positive-real realization cover or full-dimensional separator. No complexity domination over Wu et al. is claimed. The strict deliverable is staged: a complete \(p=2,q=4\) eight-branch classification, then a bounded covariance-terminal-width compiler with explicit certificates and bit complexity, followed by the all-graph open question. Independently, the terminal theorem preserves the actual rows already derived in Equation (20), replaces the invalid change-to-baseline specialization in Theorem 3.15 by terminal-copy linkage, and adds exact-support and retained-edge affine screens. No novelty claim is made for \(p=q\).

seed_details.opportunity: For \(p<q\), characterize exactly when every legal positive-real covariance branch projects densely onto the true parameter domain and when a relatively open covariance-only graph alternative remains.
seed_details.first_changed_proof_step: Replace the anchor's dimension count for one perfect-intervention fiber by the exact rank-two covariance-difference factorization, then retain shared mixing, exact support, and Schur-complement positivity across all contexts.
seed_details.destination_search: Bounded exact-title and target--method searches for overcomplete soft-intervention covariance compatibility, positive-real projection completeness, and graph-specific non-quantifier-elimination criteria found no result occupying this target.
seed_details.red_team: A cynical referee may call the result immediate from real quantifier elimination because every branch is semialgebraic.
seed_details.rebuttal: The deliverable forbids unrestricted elimination and requires a graph-specific realization-or-separator invariant with an explicit complexity bound; neither the anchor nor general semialgebraic decidability supplies that structure.

seed_details.opportunity: Replace observational-path ranks by the actual changed mechanism rows and give an if-and-only-if terminal-copy strict-gammoid plus affine-hyperplane certificate.
seed_details.first_changed_proof_step: Do not replace \((\Lambda^{(k)}-\Lambda^{(0)})\)-weighted path sums by baseline edge weights; expand minors in a graph with independent terminal copies instead.
seed_details.destination_search: Searches combining soft compatibility, actual intervention rows, terminal copies, and affine-span certificates found the anchor but no correction or complete graph algorithm.
seed_details.red_team: A cynical referee may say genericity in Theorem 3.15 already licenses the substitution.
seed_details.rebuttal: The determinant \(\gamma(\beta d-b\delta)\) is generically nonzero when the observational-path determinant is identically zero, so independent changed-row coefficients invalidate that substitution on a Zariski-open set.

seed_details.opportunity: Prove \(\mathsf{Cov}_{q}(G)=\mathsf{H}_{\mathrm{soft}}(G)\) for square mixing, uniformly over target permutations, loading signs and scales, exact supports, and positive variance chambers.
seed_details.first_changed_proof_step: Upgrade the anchor's unconstrained covariance fiber comparison to baseline whitening and inductive elimination of the alternate loading line using the recovered ancestor order.
seed_details.destination_search: The closest destination paper, SquiresSeigalBhateUhler2023, recovers the transitive closure from soft-intervention covariances under injective mixing but does not compare covariance compatibility with corrected actual-row compatibility.
seed_details.red_team: A cynical referee may regard this as a restatement of injective covariance recovery in Squires et al.
seed_details.rebuttal: Their soft-intervention result identifies only the transitive closure, whereas equality here must characterize every same-closure graph surviving all positive candidate branches and must incorporate the corrected actual rows.

seed_details.opportunity: Define the least cumulant order \(d^{\star}(G,G')\) that removes a covariance-compatible alternative, with a multi-trek minor when finite and an all-orders alternative realization otherwise.
seed_details.first_changed_proof_step: Replace fiber-degree reduction by a graph-pair separation statement; a lower-dimensional parameter fiber is not enough unless the candidate graph disappears.
seed_details.destination_search: The destination pair of multi-trek separation and overcomplete rank-one recovery is split between Robeva--Seby and Wang--Seigal; the bounded search found no coupled unknown-target LCD separation-order theorem.
seed_details.red_team: A cynical referee may say sufficiently high cumulants already recover the factor columns, so \(d^{\star}\) is bookkeeping.
seed_details.rebuttal: Factor recovery does not determine whether structural coupling and unknown target alignment eliminate a graph; proving the finite-versus-infinite dichotomy requires a new coupled invariant.

seed_details.anchor: LeyesCarrenoMeroniSeigal2025, Problem 5.2; BoegeSolus2024 is the method exemplar
seed_details.opportunity: Construct a finite birational atlas for regular covariance branches that transports every variance inequality and support inequation to observed covariance coordinates.
seed_details.first_changed_proof_step: Boege and Solus start from a globally rationally identifiable parametrization; overcomplete LCD instead requires branchwise rational inverse charts and a proof that their positive images cover the generic fiber.
seed_details.destination_search: Searches for ambirational soft-intervention LCD and branchwise positive covariance charts found no application to shared overcomplete mixing.
seed_details.red_team: A cynical referee may say this is a direct application of real birational implicitization.
seed_details.rebuttal: The LCD map is not globally birational when \(p<q\); the missing theorem is precisely finite chart coverage and gluing across nonunique positive decompositions.

seed_details.anchor: KelaVonPrillwitzAbergChavesGross2020, Proposition 2 and the converse realization section
seed_details.opportunity: Derive a hierarchy of covariance-cone face separators that is complete for selected soft-intervention graph families and returns a positive realization on acceptance.
seed_details.first_changed_proof_step: Replace independent positive-semidefinite components supported by a bipartite graph with context-coupled rank-one differences sharing one mixing matrix and one structural inverse.
seed_details.destination_search: The searched covariance-compatibility literature provides convex primal and dual certificates for bipartite latent structures, not a complete separator hierarchy for the nonconvex shared-context LCD image.
seed_details.red_team: A cynical referee may say semidefinite duality already gives every required separator.
seed_details.rebuttal: The graph-realization equations make the LCD feasible set a finite union of nonconvex projections, so the Kela et al. cone is only an outer relaxation unless branch coupling is proved complete.

seed_details.opportunity: Classify the finite forbidden terminal-reuse configurations for which the published observational-path class differs from actual-row compatibility.
seed_details.first_changed_proof_step: Compare original-terminal and copied-terminal path matroids before solving the affine child-column systems.
seed_details.destination_search: No forbidden-subgraph or matroid-minor characterization of this published class was located; the available anchor gives only rank tests.
seed_details.red_team: A cynical referee may say enumeration of all same-closure DAGs is already an exact characterization.
seed_details.rebuttal: Enumeration decides a fixed graph but does not identify the obstruction family; this seed survives only if a finite structural characterization sharper than enumeration is obtained.

seed_details.anchor: KelaVonPrillwitzAbergChavesGross2020, covariance compatibility theorem; FoygelBarberDrtonSturmaWeihs2022 is the method exemplar
seed_details.opportunity: Give a fixed-parameter tractable covariance-frontier criterion for DAGs of bounded ancestor width or bounded terminal-linkage width.
seed_details.first_changed_proof_step: Replace latent-factor half-trek recovery of one coefficient column by dynamic programming over covariance factor-line branches and terminal-copy separators.
seed_details.destination_search: The latent-factor half-trek paper proves polynomial checking only when searched latent sets are bounded and shows unrestricted checking is hard; no corresponding soft-LCD covariance-frontier algorithm was found.
seed_details.red_team: A cynical referee may call bounded width an arbitrary tractable subclass.
seed_details.rebuttal: It is defensible only if the width is the maximum terminal separator governing actual-row rank and yields a sharp complexity transition; otherwise this seed is dropped.

seed_details.anchor: KelaVonPrillwitzAbergChavesGross2020, dual witness construction in Section IV
seed_details.opportunity: Turn population covariance separators into sample-split tests for excluding soft-compatible graph alternatives while accounting for estimated factor directions.
seed_details.first_changed_proof_step: Replace a fixed convex dual witness by a branch-union separator selected on one sample and evaluated on an independent sample.
seed_details.destination_search: No finite-sample test was found for the corrected soft-LCD compatibility class; existing covariance witness proposals do not estimate overcomplete intervention factor lines.
seed_details.red_team: A cynical referee may say sample splitting after a population certificate is routine.
seed_details.rebuttal: The statistical problem is not credible until the population branch-union separator exists and its estimation stability is quantified, so this is deferred rather than padded into the core.
